section_1.title: The Hook: Geometry vs. Topology
section_1.content: Introduce the difference between 'rigid' geometry (fixed lengths/angles) and 'topological' geometry, where properties remain invariant under continuous deformation (stretching, twisting, bending) without tearing or gluing.
section_1.example: An animation showing a square being stretched into a circle; visually demonstrating that they are 'topologically equivalent'.

section_2.title: Core Concept: Homeomorphism
section_2.content: Define 'homeomorphism' as a continuous function with a continuous inverse. Explain the 'no tearing, no gluing' rule. Emphasize that holes are the fundamental 'fingerprint' of a shape.
section_2.example: A classic visual: morphing a coffee mug into a donut (torus) to show they both possess exactly one hole, making them topologically the same.

section_3.title: The Genus: Counting Holes
section_3.content: Introduce 'Genus' (g) as the number of holes. This provides a numerical invariant to classify surfaces. Explain why a sphere (g=0) cannot be turned into a torus (g=1) without cutting.
section_3.example: Animation of a flat sheet transforming into a sphere, then attempting to punch a hole to create a torus, visually explaining why this transition is impossible under topological rules.

section_4.title: Real-World Application: The Map Coloring Problem
section_4.content: Briefly connect topology to graph theory and the Four Color Theorem. Explain how topology simplifies complex networks into nodes and edges, independent of their physical map layout.
section_4.example: A complex subway map animation: shifting from a geographically accurate layout to a topological schematic where only station connections matter, not the literal distance between them.

section_5.title: Conclusion: Beyond Surfaces
section_5.content: Summarize that topology studies global properties rather than local measurements. Preview advanced topics like knots or manifolds as the next frontier.
section_5.example: A quick montage of a knot being untangled or tightened, illustrating that the knot's identity remains the same until the string is cut.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
